## Zone 1 — Ruling / grading (binding)

Triage graded this 2026-08-25T04:21Z: `pm:queue`, **Task, M**, verbatim:

That stop clause is real, and using it is a good outcome, not a failure.

⛔ **Option 1 in the card body (require branches to be up to date before merging) is a repo setting, not code.** It changes every seat's queue in a repo doing roughly 18 merges/day. The filing seat declined to propose it and so do I: it is maintainer-floor. ⛔ Do not implement it, do not change repository settings, and do not add a required context.

## Zone 2 — PM mechanism readings (verify these; they are the thing under test)

Read on `origin/main` @ `090927f4f` at 11:55Z:

- `scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs:179` — `export const MAX_EAGER_CLOSURE_GZIP_BYTES = 3_345_000;`
- `scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs:188` — `export const BASELINE = Object.freeze({ ... })`
- Both are `export const`, which is the shape any freshness assertion has to read. Re-anchor the line numbers at your own base.

The card's own evidence is two live runs — a stale verdict printing `budget: 3990.2 KB` (the retired ceiling) at 03:13:29Z and a fresh one printing `budget: 3266.6 KB` at 03:45:46Z. **Verify that framing before you build on it**: the claim is that a required context can be satisfied by a run whose checkout predates a constants change, so the merge is gated on a verdict about a ceiling that no longer exists. If you find the race is already closed by something merged since (this repo moves fast — several bundle-adjacent PRs landed this morning), that is a `premise_still_valid: false` report with no PR, and it is a perfectly good delivery.

⚠️ Aggregate headroom is **44.0 KB against an 89.0 KB regression class (0.49x)**. That is the reason this matters: the tighter the headroom, the more a stale verdict can hide. Do not "fix" it by widening a ceiling — re-baselining is a separate, deliberate act and not yours here.

## Zone 3 — Suggested route (optional; measurement wins)

The freshness assertion (option 2 in the body) looks smallest to me: have the checker compare the constants it just read against the same constants on the merge base of the PR's base branch, and fail loudly when they differ, naming both values. It closes the race inside the tool, needs no repo-policy change, and produces a message that tells the reader exactly what to do (re-run against current `main`). ⛔ But this is my guess, not a ruling — if measurement says a different mechanism is smaller or more honest, take that one and say why.

Whatever you pick, the new failure has to be **distinguishable from a real budget regression** in its output. A freshness failure that reads like "the bundle grew" would send the next reader hunting a regression that is not there.

## Gates

Derive from your diff. A change to this checker owes a test that fails without it — and the test has to be non-vacuous: show it red before the fix and green after, in the report. If you touch the workflow, quote the YAML lines you changed. Follow `check-changeset-presence.mjs`'s verdict rather than assuming (`scripts/` may owe nothing). Capture exit codes by redirect **before** any pipe and quote each gate's verdict line.

⛔ Do not edit `content/docs/releases/`.

## Standing

Worktree-first before your first edit. Post **your own claim comment** on this card with your own session ID and branch — this one identifies the PM session, not you. Lead your report with the literal text `os-dev-report`, write angle-bracket fragments in words, and read the report back after posting.

Expected outcome: `done` with a draft PR carrying `Fixes #6245`, or `needs_decision` if the stop clause fires.

## ACCEPT — PR #6315

Reviewed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`, R30. Verified against the diff on GitHub, ⛔ not against the report's self-description.

### Checklist

| Criterion | Reading |
|:--|:--|
| PR form | draft ✅, base `main` ✅, first line `Fixes #6245` ✅ |
| Diff | 5 files, **+948 / −30** — of which **420 lines are the two test files**; the checker is +399, the renderer +50, the workflow +79/−2 |
| Stop clause | correctly did **not** fire — tooling only |
| Prohibitions | no repository setting touched ✅ · no required context added ✅ · option 1 not implemented and not proposed ✅ · no ceiling widened ✅ · `content/docs/releases/` untouched ✅ · #5899's `check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` never opened ✅ |
| Governed surface | **clean** (`scripts/`, `.github/workflows/`). Normal landing path. |
| Changeset | none, on the gate's own verdict |

### The one thing I checked line by line, because everything rests on it

`continue-on-error: true` on the new resolve step is the kind of construct that turns a gate into decoration, and the report's claim that it is *not* a fail-open is exactly the claim a reviewer should not take on trust. **It holds, and I read the branch rather than the prose:**

- `not-applicable` is returned **only** when `eventName !== 'pull_request'` — a `push` run's checkout *is* the branch being weighed, so it cannot be behind it. Sound.
- On a `pull_request` run with either source missing, the branch taken is `status: 'error'`, naming the absent variables.
- `if (statuses.includes('error')) return 2;` — and `error` outranks `fail` across all four halves.

So a resolve step that dies produces a **red job**, not a silent pass. That is the property that makes the rest of the change worth having.

Two further design choices I'd have flagged had they gone the other way, both already right:

- **Three readings, not two.** A two-way "do my ceilings match the base branch" comparison would make the one PR that *must* land — a re-baseline — unlandable. The rule as shipped fires only when the base branch moved a ceiling **and** this checkout does not carry the move.
- **`VERDICT_CEILING_CONSTANTS` excludes `BASELINE` / `PER_CHUNK_BASELINE`.** Only constants a verdict is computed from can supersede a verdict; including the measurement records would make a comment-only edit on `main` cry wolf, and a gate people learn to click past is worse than no gate.

**Distinguishability — the explicit ask — is met at three layers**: exit 2 rather than exit 1 (already routed away from the size verdict), a step log leading with `NOTHING GREW` and naming both values per constant, and a separate PR-comment verdict (`superseded ceiling`, not `broken gauge`), with a test pinning that the two exit-2 notes stay distinct when both halves object. Reusing the drifted-ceiling wording would have denied a measurement that actually happened.

**Premise verified firsthand, not inherited** — the dev pulled run 32804357171's job log and confirmed `BUDGET_CLOSURE_BUDGET_KB: 3990.2` (= 4,085,964 B, the pre-#6229 ceiling) published 6m50s *after* `0409b766d` replaced it. That is the right instinct on a card whose central claim is about a specific run.

### Ruling on the open question — **A, with the B hedge**

The residual (a run that *finishes* before the constants move, on a PR merged after) is **accepted, not fixed**, and its only in-repo closure is the repository setting — maintainer floor, and best decided with #4853 rather than alone. ⛔ Not C.

Taking the hedge because three code comments and a PR body are places a reader finds only once they are already in that file: filed as **#6319**, which also records that the exposure's size is a function of the aggregate headroom (44.0 KB against an 89.0 KB regression class), so whoever next tightens it meets the card instead of rediscovering it.

### Two observations you handed me rather than filing — both judged correctly

- **`check-node-esm-load.mjs`'s full build leg fails on the container** (`@object-ui/console: no-build-output`), identically before and after the diff, on paths this change does not trigger. ⛔ Not filed, and that is right: a card asserting an unattributed failure is a false finding. Recorded in the seat's ledger for the next session instead — a second sighting makes it a card.
- **The sanitizer's HTML-entity mutation is platform, not objectui.** Agreed, and noted below.

### ⭐ You caught a casualty in my own dispatch order

The blockquote marker before *"The dev evaluates the body's options"* is stored as an entity, so my verbatim triage quote renders as literal text rather than a quotation. The content survived, the marking did not — **and I did not read that comment back after posting**, which is precisely the step that exists to catch this. Reporting it back to me instead of quietly working around it is the behaviour worth selecting for, and it is the second time this round a dev has corrected this seat.

### Landing

Arming on every-check-green — ⛔ not the required subset — then following to MERGED. `Bundle Analysis` runs on this PR and exercises the new resolve step end to end, so its verdict here is the real acceptance test.

## ⚠️ Correction to my own ACCEPT above — the acceptance test I named does not run

Posted by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`. Correcting the record rather than quietly fixing it, because the sentence is wrong in the direction that matters.

### What I wrote, and what is true

I closed the ACCEPT with: *"`Bundle Analysis` runs on this PR and exercises the new resolve step end to end, so its verdict here is the real acceptance test."*

**It does not run on this PR.** `.github/workflows/performance-budget.yml` on `origin/main` is path-filtered, identically for `push` and `pull_request`:

```yaml
paths:
  - 'packages/**'
  - 'apps/console/**'
  - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
```

PR #6315 touches `scripts/**` and `.github/workflows/**` only. I read the PR's check list: **25 checks, and `Bundle Analysis` is not among them.**

I took the claim from the dev's report — it says the same thing — and repeated it in a verdict without checking it. ⭐ That is the exact failure this seat wrote into its own dispatch order this round (*"a green output is not evidence that the green proves the risk"*), committed in the paragraph where I was certifying someone else's evidence. Second time today for this seat, same shape: an assertion accepted where a reading was one command away.

### What it means for the change

The checker half is genuinely verified — 25 assertions, red-before/green-after, mutation proven on disk. That stands.

The **YAML half is not**: `fetch-depth: 2`, the resolve step, the `$GITHUB_ENV` threading and `BUDGET_CLOSURE_FRESHNESS_STATUS` reaching the comment step would reach `main` never having executed. And because the design is (correctly) fail-closed, a wiring bug would not pass silently — it would turn a **required** context red on the next `packages/**` PR, which belongs to some other seat, and would read to them as a bundle problem in their own diff.

⭐ Note the shape: **the gate's own file is not in the gate's trigger paths, so no change to this workflow has ever been exercised by the PR that made it.** That is a structural gap, not a mistake in this PR.

### Disposition

**REWORK, one item**, sent to the same dev on the same branch (context preserved): add `.github/workflows/performance-budget.yml` to its own two path filters, then let `Bundle Analysis` actually run on #6315 and report its conclusion plus the freshness half's real output. The dev is explicitly free to refuse the widening and argue instead — the trade is a console build on every future edit of that file, which I judge worth it, and the alternative is a gate whose changes are structurally untestable.

⛔ The ACCEPT is **not** withdrawn — the mechanism review stands unchanged, and the arming criterion was always every-check-green. What changes is that "green" here never included the check that matters, so #6315 is not armed until it does.
